commit_message:
Bug 1948203 - Skip alt-svc validation if we already connected to the server, r=necko-reviewers,jesup

This patch optimizes how Firefox handles speculative connections for alt-svc headers. When a server sends an alt-svc header, Firefox normally creates a speculative connection to validate it. With this patch, if the connection’s hash key matches the one generated from the alt-svc header, the validation step is skipped since an equivalent connection is already in place, avoiding unnecessary work.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D238218

fix_commit.message: Bug 1951554 - Avoid racing on nsHttpTransaction::mConnInfo, r=necko-reviewers,valentin
fix_commit.author: Kershaw Chang

findings.title: Data race on mConnInfo between GetConnInfo and DisableHttp3
findings.message: The `GetConnInfo()` method reads `mConnInfo` on the main thread without holding a lock, while `DisableHttp3()` modifies `mConnInfo` via `mConnInfo.swap(connInfo)` on the socket thread. This creates a data race condition. The ThreadSanitizer detected a read of size 8 on the main thread in `GetConnInfo` concurrent with a write of size 8 on thread T7 in `DisableHttp3`. This can lead to use-after-free or reading corrupted pointer values, potentially causing crashes or undefined behavior.
findings.suggestion: Access to mConnInfo must be synchronized. The fix introduces a `mFinalizedConnInfo` member that is a clone of `mConnInfo` taken when the transaction is activated. This finalized copy is accessed under mutex protection via `TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo()`, avoiding the race with DisableHttp3's modification of the original mConnInfo.

findings.title: Unprotected access to shared mConnInfo member
findings.message: The `GetConnInfo()` method in `nsHttpTransaction` accesses the `mConnInfo` member variable without any synchronization primitive (mutex lock). This is called from the main thread in `ContinueProcessResponse1()`, but `mConnInfo` can be modified by `DisableHttp3()` running on the socket thread via `mConnInfo.swap(connInfo)`. The RefPtr::Clone() operation dereferences the pointer, which races with the swap operation that modifies the pointer itself.
findings.suggestion: Add mutex protection when accessing mConnInfo, or use a separate finalized copy that's taken at a safe point during transaction activation and accessed under lock protection.

ground_truth.root_cause: Bug 1948203 introduced a new call to mTransaction->GetConnInfo() in nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1() on the main thread to pass connection information to ProcessAltService(). However, mConnInfo in nsHttpTransaction was already being modified by DisableHttp3() on the socket thread without synchronization. The pre-existing code paths didn't have this cross-thread access pattern, making the race condition a regression introduced by this optimization patch.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable code path at lines 2749-2750 where mTransaction->GetConnInfo() is called on the main thread without synchronization. This newly introduced call reads mConnInfo that can be concurrently modified on the socket thread, creating the data race.

Performs unsynchronized read of mConnInfo member variable on the main thread. This read operation races with DisableHttp3's write on the socket thread, potentially reading a corrupted pointer or use-after-free.
Modifies mConnInfo via mConnInfo.swap(connInfo) on the socket thread without holding a lock. This write operation creates the race condition with GetConnInfo's read on the main thread.

The function that receives the nsHttpConnectionInfo* parameter from GetConnInfo() call and is the reason for introducing the vulnerable cross-thread access. Understanding this context shows why the optimization was added and why it's unsafe.
